title: Cryostat Sectioning of Tissues for 3D Multimodal Molecular Imaging
author: David Anderson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bt8inrue
materials: Adjust the section thickness setting to 10μm.

steps.title: Set cryostat temperatures
steps.instruction: Program the cryostat to an internal temperature of -21 °C and set the object (sample) temperature to between -10 °C and -20 °C, choosing the exact value based on the tissue type.

steps.title: Prepare the microtome blade
steps.instruction: Remove the blade from its container, wipe it with ethanol and a lint‑free wipe, then insert it into the cryostat and lock it in place.

steps.title: Mount tissue in OCT
steps.instruction: Place the tissue onto the cryostat chuck using optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound in the desired orientation; if needed, shave a flat surface onto the mounting area with a razor blade to improve orientation and adherence.

steps.title: Adjust stage angle
steps.instruction: Tilt the stage to provide a less acute passage of the tissue over the blade, avoiding acute angles that cause surrounding CMC to fragment and lose structural integrity.

steps.title: Trim CMC to expose tissue
steps.instruction: Trim the surrounding carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) using larger section increments of 30–50 µm until the tissue becomes visible.

steps.title: Replace blade before imaging
steps.instruction: Before cutting sections for imaging, replace the blade because trimming dulls it and reduces section quality.

steps.title: Remove excess CMC
steps.instruction: If excess CMC remains around the visible tissue, carefully remove it with a precooled razor blade.

steps.title: Position anti‑roll bar
steps.instruction: Set the anti‑roll bar so it is close enough to stabilize the tissue but not so far toward the sample that it scrapes the tissue.

steps.title: Section tissue to desired count
steps.instruction: Continue sectioning until the process is reproducible and consistent, then collect the required number of sections.

steps.title: Collect serial sections on slide
steps.instruction: Place each successive section onto the same slide for 3‑D imaging, recording any "lost" sections because they affect later data reconstruction.

steps.title: Position sections on target surface
steps.instruction: Using a fine‑tipped paint brush, manipulate each section onto the target surface (regular slide or ITO slide) while keeping it on the surrounding CMC material to avoid contamination or disruption.

steps.title: Flatten sections with Teflon slide
steps.instruction: When all sections are on the slide, invert the slide and gently press a Teflon‑coated slide onto the tissues to prevent wrinkles; flat sections thaw‑mount better than wrinkled ones, which can stretch, fold, and create imaging artifacts.

steps.title: Thaw‑mount and dry sections
steps.instruction: Thaw‑mount the sections by applying heat from a gloved hand or by using a slide warmer set to 20 °C; immediately air‑dry the sections before returning the sample to the cryostat or a vacuum desiccator. Note: use indium tin oxide (ITO)‑coated slides for imaging mass spectrometry and poly‑lysine‑coated coverslips for CODEX immunofluorescence.

steps.title: Store sections appropriately
steps.instruction: If analysis will occur within 24 hours, store the sections in a desiccator; for longer‑term storage, keep them at -80 °C in a vacuum‑sealed slide holder.
